question: The Central Government approved the allocation of additional how many million tonnes of rice from the Food Corporation of India (FCI) for ethanol production in May 2025?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**2.8 million tonnes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In May **2025**, the **Central Government** approved the allocation of an additional **2.8 million tonnes of rice** from the **Food Corporation of India (FCI)** for ethanol production.
 
• This decision is part of India's efforts to achieve **energy independence** and promote **biofuel production**.
 
• **Ethanol** is a renewable fuel derived from agricultural products, including rice, which is used in blending with petrol to reduce dependency on crude oil imports.
 
• The policy aligns with the **National Bio-Energy Mission**, focusing on reducing the carbon footprint and enhancing sustainable energy solutions.
 
• India aims to achieve a blending target of **20% ethanol in petrol by 2025**, known as the **E20 target**.
 
• The allocation of rice from FCI supports the strategy to utilize surplus food grains for biofuel production, ensuring minimal wastage and promoting efficient use of resources.
 
• This initiative fosters **sustainable development**, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthens the rural economy by creating demand for agricultural produce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Food Corporation of India (FCI)**__

 __
 
• The **Food Corporation of India** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution**.
 
• Established in **1965**, FCI ensures food security by procuring, storing, and distributing food grains across India.
 
• It maintains buffer stocks of food grains and regulates market prices to ensure availability and affordability.
 
 
 
• **National Bio-Energy Mission**__
 __
 
• The **National Bio-Energy Mission** emphasizes the development of biofuels such as ethanol, biodiesel, and bio-CNG.
 
• It aims to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, mitigate climate change, and enhance rural livelihoods.
 
• The mission is aligned with India's **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the Paris Agreement to combat climate change.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Ethanol Blending**__
 
 
• **Ethanol blending** reduces crude oil imports, saving foreign exchange reserves.
 
• It is a cleaner fuel that reduces **carbon emissions**, contributing to environmental sustainability.
 
• Promoting ethanol production also supports farmers by utilizing surplus grains and diversifying their income sources.
